description: Tuju is one of São Paulo's two historic three-Michelin-star restaurants and a defining address for contemporary Brazilian fine dining. Ivan Ralston's team uses Brazilian biomes, seasonality and a striking multi-level house to turn dinner into a full destination experience. It is essential for affluent diners who want the city's most current global benchmark rather than a classic-only itinerary.
highlights: Three-star Brazilian tasting menu, architectural Pinheiros setting, Latin America 50 Best recognition
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery

description: Evvai is Luiz Filipe Souza's refined dialogue between Italian heritage and Brazilian ingredients, now at the very top of Latin American fine dining. The Oriundi menu gives the experience a personal narrative, supported by polished service and one of the most ambitious kitchens in the city. Its Michelin, 50 Best and La Liste recognition make it a mandatory São Paulo reservation.
highlights: Three Michelin stars, Brazilian-Italian tasting menu, La Liste 2026 top-tier recognition
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; La Liste; Exame

description: D.O.M. remains Alex Atala's flagship and one of the restaurants that put modern Brazilian gastronomy into the global conversation. The cooking draws on Amazonian and Brazilian ingredients with a cerebral but luxurious point of view. For international diners, it is still the classic São Paulo fine-dining address to understand before exploring the newer generation.
highlights: Two Michelin stars, Amazonian ingredients, iconic Brazilian fine-dining institution
sources: Michelin Guide; Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; CNN Brasil

description: A Casa do Porco is São Paulo's most famous democratic dining phenomenon, but its influence is far more serious than the relaxed room suggests. Janaína Torres and Jefferson Rueda turn pork, vegetables, sustainability and downtown energy into one of Brazil's most recognizable restaurant experiences. It belongs in the high-end core because it is a current global 50 Best name and a restaurant sophisticated travelers actively plan around.
highlights: World 50 Best recognition, pork-focused tasting menu, downtown São Paulo energy
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; La Liste; 50 Best Discovery

description: Maní is Helena Rizzo and Willem Vandeven's elegant Brazilian restaurant in a warm Jardim Paulistano house. The kitchen balances organic ingredients, refined technique and a distinctly Brazilian sensibility without losing the relaxed charm that made it internationally loved. It remains one of the city's most important Michelin-starred dining rooms.
highlights: Michelin-starred Brazilian cuisine, garden-house atmosphere, long-running international reputation
sources: Michelin Guide; Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; Restaurant Maní; Veja São Paulo

description: Nelita has become one of São Paulo's most persuasive contemporary Italian restaurants, led by chef Tássia Magalhães and an all-female kitchen team. The room feels stylish but not stiff, while the menus combine Italian memory with Brazilian produce and personal storytelling. Its high ranking in Latin America's 50 Best makes it one of the city's strongest non-starred global names.
highlights: Latin America's 50 Best No. 12, contemporary Italian cooking, warm Pinheiros atmosphere
sources: Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; Michelin Guide; 50 Best Discovery; Veja São Paulo

description: Ryo Gastronomia is Edson Yamashita's highly disciplined Japanese restaurant in Itaim Bibi. The experience is built around kaiseki precision, sushi technique and a serious sense of ritual. It is one of São Paulo's most polished Japanese fine-dining reservations.
highlights: Michelin-starred Japanese kaiseki, omakase counter, rigorous technique
sources: Michelin Guide; Ryo Gastronomia; Veja São Paulo

description: Jun Sakamoto is one of São Paulo's most enduring sushi counters and still one of the purest Japanese luxury experiences in the city. The hidden, low-signage room places the chef and the fish at the center of the evening. It is a natural choice for diners seeking a classic omakase rather than a broader contemporary menu.
highlights: Michelin-starred omakase, discreet Pinheiros room, benchmark nigiri counter
sources: Michelin Guide; Jun Sakamoto; Cidade de São Paulo

description: Tangará Jean-Georges brings polished luxury-hotel dining to Palácio Tangará, one of São Paulo's most refined urban resorts. The kitchen carries the Jean-Georges Vongerichten signature while adapting the experience to Brazilian produce and a grand hotel setting. It is especially relevant for business, romantic and hotel-based special-occasion dinners.
highlights: Michelin-starred luxury hotel dining, Palácio Tangará setting, polished international service
sources: Michelin Guide; Palácio Tangará; Oetker Collection

description: Kuro is a sleek, intimate Japanese restaurant focused on seasonal fish, omakase structure and a minimalist sense of luxury. The restaurant's Michelin star reflects a citywide appetite for high-end Japanese counters that are precise but not showy. It works especially well for diners who want a refined, seafood-driven evening in Jardins.
highlights: Michelin-starred omakase, seasonal fish, intimate Jardins setting
sources: Michelin Guide; Kuro e Shiro; Cidade de São Paulo; Veja São Paulo

description: Kinoshita is a São Paulo Japanese classic whose kappo cooking and refined service have kept it relevant through multiple Michelin cycles. The restaurant is also notable for its serious champagne culture and status as a Krug Ambassade. It is a strong choice for diners who want Japanese technique in a more spacious, polished dining room.
highlights: Michelin-starred kappo cuisine, Krug Ambassade, Vila Nova Conceição polish
sources: Michelin Guide; Kinoshita; Veja São Paulo

description: Kazuo Harada's restaurant gives São Paulo a polished Pan-Asian and Japanese-influenced fine-dining address. The Michelin-starred kitchen is expressive and visually precise, with a clientele that understands it as more than a conventional sushi restaurant. It adds breadth to the city's Japanese luxury scene.
highlights: Michelin-starred Pan-Asian cuisine, refined tasting menus, Jardim Europa location
sources: Michelin Guide; Kazuo Restaurante; Veja São Paulo

description: KANOE is one of São Paulo's most intimate omakase rooms, serving only a very small number of guests per seating. Tadashi Shiraishi's counter focuses on Edo-style sushi, aged fish and a sense of quiet concentration. Its Michelin star and eight-seat format make it one of the city's most exclusive Japanese dinners.
highlights: Michelin-starred eight-seat omakase, Edo-style sushi, highly intimate format
sources: Michelin Guide; KANOE; Tock

description: Murakami is chef Tsuyoshi Murakami's personal Japanese restaurant, known for a daily-changing tasting menu and a performative counter-led experience. The cooking is expressive while remaining ingredient-focused, giving the restaurant a different personality from São Paulo's more restrained sushi rooms. It is a Michelin-starred choice for diners who want personality with their omakase.
highlights: Michelin-starred Japanese tasting menu, chef-led counter energy, daily-changing experience
sources: Michelin Guide; Murakami; Cidade de São Paulo; Veja São Paulo

description: Oizumi Sushi is a Michelin-starred omakase focused on fish maturity, texture and the precision of sushi technique. The restaurant offers both counter seating and small private rooms, which makes it useful for affluent diners who want discretion as well as culinary focus. It is one of the city's newer serious Japanese references.
highlights: Michelin-starred dry-aged fish omakase, private rooms, technical sushi focus
sources: Michelin Guide; Oizumi Sushi; ViaMichelin

description: Kan Suke is a small, highly focused Michelin-starred Japanese counter in Paraíso. The restaurant's strength is its stripped-back concentration on sushi, sashimi, speed, rice and ingredient quality rather than spectacle. It is for diners who value authenticity and craft over a luxury-room production.
highlights: Michelin-starred sushi counter, intimate Paraíso setting, ingredient-first technique
sources: Michelin Guide; ViaMichelin; En Primeur Club

description: Picchi is Pier Paolo Picchi's Michelin-starred Italian restaurant on Rua Oscar Freire. The cooking starts from classic Italian reference points and tightens them with contemporary technique and Brazilian ingredients. Its Jardins address and polished hotel-adjacent room make it a reliable luxury Italian choice.
highlights: Michelin-starred Italian cuisine, Oscar Freire location, Regent Park setting
sources: Michelin Guide; Picchi; Veja São Paulo

description: Fame Osteria is one of São Paulo's most intimate Michelin-starred Italian experiences, hidden behind a discreet Oscar Freire doorway. Marco and Erika Renzetti run a small, reservation-led room where the tasting menu, handmade pasta and wine service are the point of the evening. It is special-occasion dining without grand-hotel formality.
highlights: Michelin-starred hidden osteria, tiny tasting-menu room, strong wine service
sources: Michelin Guide; 50 Best Discovery; Veja São Paulo

description: Terraço NOTIÊ brings Onildo Rocha's biome-driven Brazilian cooking to a rooftop setting above the historic center. The restaurant offers tasting menus alongside a broader terrace and music-driven hospitality complex, but the dinner offer is serious enough for São Paulo's luxury dining set. Its view over the city center gives it a setting few tasting-menu restaurants can match.
highlights: Brazilian biome tasting menus, rooftop over the historic center, Michelin-selected address
sources: Michelin Guide; Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; Veja São Paulo

description: Kotori is Thiago Bañares' sleek Japanese-yōshoku restaurant in Pinheiros, more relaxed than a starched omakase but still highly deliberate. The food connects Japanese comfort, Brazilian ingredients and cocktail-bar energy in a design-conscious room. Its 50 Best regional profile and Michelin Bib Gourmand status make it a strong high-end casual counterpoint to the city's formal Japanese restaurants.
highlights: Latin America 50 Best recognition, yōshoku cooking, creative cocktails and design-led room
sources: Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; Michelin Guide; Tock

description: Metzi is one of São Paulo's most distinctive contemporary restaurants, connecting Mexican technique with Brazilian produce. Luana Sabino and Eduardo Nava Ortiz have built a precise, minimalist room whose tasting menu feels singular in the city. It is a compelling instead-of-Michelin option for diners seeking a modern Latin American point of view.
highlights: Contemporary Mexican-Brazilian tasting menu, chef-driven Pinheiros room, 50 Best recognition
sources: Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; Michelin Guide; Veja São Paulo

description: Cepa has become a Pinheiros favorite for contemporary, market-driven cooking with a wine-minded, urban feel. The current location gives the restaurant more comfort and scale while preserving the chef-driven energy that made it hard to book. It is less formal than the Michelin-starred tasting rooms but still clears the affluent dinner bar.
highlights: Farm-to-table Michelin Bib Gourmand, strong wine energy, Pinheiros buzz
sources: Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants; Michelin Guide; Veja São Paulo; São Paulo Secreto

description: A Figueira Rubaiyat is one of São Paulo's most enduring affluent-room restaurants, built around a spectacular fig tree in Jardins. The Rubaiyat group's premium meat, seafood and wine formula makes it a concierge-safe choice for business dinners, family celebrations and visitors who want a grand local classic. It is not avant-garde, but it is unmistakably part of the city's luxury dining fabric.
highlights: Grand fig-tree dining room, premium meats and seafood, long-running Jardins classic
sources: Michelin Guide; Rubaiyat Group; Cidade de São Paulo; En Primeur Club

description: Fasano is São Paulo's archetypal luxury Italian dining room, a polished classic inside the Fasano orbit in Jardins. The wine cellar, service and old-world atmosphere give the restaurant a sense of permanence that few newer rooms can match. It is a natural booking for diners who want elegance, discretion and high Italian gastronomy rather than novelty.
highlights: Luxury Italian flagship, serious wine cellar, polished Jardins hotel service
sources: Michelin Guide; Fasano; Michelin Key Hotels; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Taraz brings Felipe Bronze's South American fire-led cooking into the Rosewood São Paulo's dramatic Matarazzo complex. The room, garden setting and hotel architecture make it one of the city's strongest design-led social dinners. It is especially relevant for affluent travelers staying around Paulista, Jardins and the Rosewood itself.
highlights: Rosewood São Paulo setting, South American fire cooking, olive-garden terrace
sources: Michelin Guide; Rosewood São Paulo; Veja São Paulo

description: Osso is Peruvian butcher-chef Renzo Garibaldi's meat-focused São Paulo restaurant, built around dry-aged cuts, fire and a sharper culinary point of view than a conventional steakhouse. It gives the city a premium grill option with chef credibility and a serious dining-room feel. For affluent diners, it is one of the more distinctive alternatives to a classic churrascaria or hotel steakhouse.
highlights: Dry-aged meat, Peruvian master butcher, Michelin-selected Itaim Bibi room
sources: Michelin Guide; Osso; Veja São Paulo; En Primeur Club

description: Emiliano is a polished luxury-hotel restaurant on Oscar Freire, with understated service and a wine-driven hospitality style. The kitchen is contemporary and elegant rather than headline-grabbing, making it useful for a quieter high-end dinner. It belongs on the list because the hotel, location and service level all map directly to the affluent São Paulo dining market.
highlights: Oscar Freire luxury hotel dining, elegant wine program, discreet service
sources: Michelin Guide; Hotel Emiliano; Veja São Paulo; Michelin Key Hotels

description: Amadeus is São Paulo's classic upscale seafood restaurant, long associated with refined fish, shrimp and shellfish cooking in Jardins. The house has the confidence of an institution rather than a trend, with a menu built for sharing, wine and polished service. It is the obvious seafood inclusion for affluent diners who want a São Paulo classic outside the tasting-menu circuit.
highlights: Classic upscale seafood, oysters and Brazilian fish dishes, Michelin-selected address
sources: Michelin Guide; Amadeus; Veja São Paulo; Tripadvisor

description: Vista Restaurante sits on the terrace of the Museum of Contemporary Art, giving São Paulo one of its strongest skyline-and-Ibirapuera dining settings. Marcelo Corrêa Bastos' menu emphasizes contemporary Brazilian flavors from across the country. It is an important affluent choice when atmosphere, architecture and city views matter as much as the food.
highlights: MAC USP rooftop, panoramic city view, contemporary Brazilian cooking
sources: Michelin Guide; Vista Restaurante; Veja São Paulo; Tripadvisor

description: Les Présidents is Érick Jacquin's theatrical French restaurant in Cerqueira César, combining classic bistro references with a high-design, high-attention room. It is expensive, sought-after and unmistakably aimed at diners who want a social, polished night out. The restaurant rounds out the list's grand French and celebrity-chef archetype.
highlights: Michelin-selected French bistro, Érick Jacquin, dramatic black-and-red dining room
sources: Michelin Guide; Veja São Paulo; En Primeur Club

description: Mocotó is Rodrigo Oliveira's celebrated Northeastern Brazilian institution in Vila Medeiros. It is relaxed and inclusive, but the cooking has enough cultural importance and culinary credibility to attract chefs, locals and international food travelers. For a more informal night, it is one of São Paulo's essential local experiences.
highlights: Northeastern Brazilian institution, Bib Gourmand, famous dadinhos de tapioca and carne de sol
sources: Michelin Guide; Mocotó; Veja São Paulo

description: Bar da Dona Onça is Janaína Rueda's lively restaurant in the Copan building, rooted in downtown São Paulo and paulistano comfort food. It is more relaxed than the high-end core, but the cooking, cocktails and cultural setting make it highly relevant to sophisticated visitors. The room captures the center's creative, bohemian energy better than a formal dining room could.
highlights: Copan building setting, paulistano comfort food, lively cocktails and downtown culture
sources: Michelin Guide; Bar da Dona Onça; Veja São Paulo

description: Tordesilhas is Mara Salles' long-running restaurant devoted to Brazilian regional foodways and traditional preparations. The room is relaxed but adult, the cooking is researched, and the menu gives travelers a broad view of Brazil beyond São Paulo's Japanese, Italian and tasting-menu scenes. It is a protected local favorite because its cultural role is stronger than its formality.
highlights: Brazilian regional classics, Mara Salles, Bib Gourmand and OAD recognition
sources: Michelin Guide; Tordesilhas; En Primeur Club

description: Jardim de Napoli is a São Paulo Italian-Brazilian classic, best known as the house of polpettone. The room is old-school, loyal and relaxed, but the culinary identity is deeply paulistano and more meaningful than a generic casual dinner. It gives affluent visitors a living snapshot of the city's Italian immigrant dining culture.
highlights: Historic polpettone institution, old-school Italian-Brazilian comfort, multigenerational local following
sources: Veja São Paulo; local restaurant references; Tripadvisor

description: Famiglia Mancini is one of São Paulo's most recognizable Italian-Brazilian cantinas, anchoring Rua Avanhandava since 1980. It is generous, theatrical and sometimes crowded, but that is part of its cultural value as a city institution. For a relaxed night, it gives affluent visitors a classic São Paulo immigrant-dining experience rather than another polished hotel room.
highlights: Historic Italian cantina, Rua Avanhandava atmosphere, family-style southern Italian cooking
sources: Famiglia Mancini; Veja São Paulo; Tripadvisor
